reviews.rationale: The entire numbered V1 on PDF46 is represented, including the star before trees and the paired daggers around the second-person made clause. The submitted source and explanation correctly preserve the break between that corrupt construction and the living-forever phrase. I cannot independently approve a grammatical continuous English sentence from the selected print. The candidate honestly retains an awkward held draft instead of silently substituting a third-person creator or Charles apparatus11 repair. This is a whole-unit source/translation hold, not a rejection of the observed trees/foliage words.

I compared the complete numbered2 on PDF46: works before him year by year, their obedience to him, negative change verb, and the accordance-with-God-ordained clause are all present. The English keeps the works as the continuing subject and preserves the negative; it neither adds a seasonal proposition from chapter IV nor deletes the closing all/everything clause. Source pages and empty notes match this unit. Minor terminal-stop normalization is disclosed in the source note.

The actual numbered3 on PDF46 is only the short two-line seas-and-rivers unit. The source, English and empty notes faithfully preserve seeing, the two water nouns, together and completing their work. My own source-first provisional summer/heat observation is expressly withdrawn in the correction artifact: it belonged to preceding IV continuation, not V3. This acceptance is based on the correctly bounded actual V3 rather than that mistaken provisional bullet.

I checked all four main-text lines on PDF46 through the no-peace close. The English preserves second-person failure to persevere/keep the command, transgression, great harsh words against his greatness, impure mouths, dry-hearted accusation, and the final negative peace statement. Actual Dillmann col1015 supports perseverance/constancy; col301 supports impurity; col1095 gives the harsh/hard/rough range of the selected adjective with Eno5:4 citation; cols322-323 support peace. The lexical footnote is proportionate and does not silently exchange dry for hard. The main-text star embedded before mouth remains in source, distinguished from apparatus superscripts.

I checked the full numbered5 on PDF46, including the parenthesized years-of-destruction expression and the star within the life-your sequence. The English keeps cursing days, ruining years of life, increase under everlasting curse and no mercy. The parenthetical expression is translated only as the selected critical print and explicitly explained as supplied according to Charles Greek witness, agreeing with personally viewed printed8 apparatus37. The note does not claim universal Ge’ez manuscript attestation or silently treat the supplied phrase as unmarked inherited text. Actual Dillmann col316 supports curse/imprecation. This is acceptance of that disclosed critical treatment.

I checked the whole numbered6 on PDF48. Three actual printed dots precede the final fragments; these are not three unread source glyphs. The final daggered association construction remains corrupt, and Charles apparatus7-9 offers repairs rather than a secure continuous selected sentence. Actual Dillmann col316 supports curse but cannot supply the lost construction. The submitted source, literal fragmentary English, low confidence, structured hold and anchored explanation are honest. I cannot lift the hold or approve a fluent restored curse/oath formula from these photographs.

I checked the complete three-line numbered7 on PDF48: chosen recipients, light/joy/peace, their inheritance of the earth, and the contrasting curse for the wicked addressees remain. Actual Dillmann cols316,322-323 and1350 support curse, peace and joy respectively. The source has no erased negative or missing continuation; English does not conflate the chosen and wicked subjects or turn the curse into a blessing. Empty footnotes introduce no additional unsupported assertion.

I checked the complete numbered8 through the final wisdom word on PDF48. Wisdom given to the chosen, their life, no renewed sin through wickedness or pride, and humble submission of those who have wisdom are represented. Actual Dillmann col757 supports sin with explicit Hen5:8 usage; col988 gives pride/arrogance; cols1229-1230 wisdom; col1179 gives humble/submissive reverence and the relevant Eno5:8 use. Personally viewed printed10 apparatus15 labels the opening an emendation, accurately disclosed by source uncertainty and anchored explanation. No claim of unanimous manuscript wording is made.

I checked the entire PDF48-to50 span, not only the initial no-sin/no-judgment clauses: all six continuation lines on50 end before VI. The source preserves all three continuation stars and both death/punishment and not-by-wrath expressions. Actual Dillmann col757 supports sin, col422 punishment/chastisement/calamity, cols1350 and322-323 joy and peace. The English keeps the judgment verb rather than adopting the alternate no-sin reading discussed in printed10 apparatus24, preserves completing the number of days and peaceful longevity, and includes increase of joy throughout life. The two anchored explanations accurately disclose that alternative and printed12 apparatus2 conjecture without silently adopting punishment-of-death wording. My earlier two-star provisional count is expressly corrected to three. This is a complete selected-print acceptance, not an assertion about every manuscript.
